Commentary.Commentary: The Pakistani bowlers tried their best but couldn't take wickets at regular intervals. The hosts were reading the deliveries properly and didn't let Pakistan get on top in this innings. Mohammad Amir, Sohail Khan and Yasir Shah got two wickets each. Let's see how their batters respond now. Pakistan will have to chase down a record total at this venue to win this match. Can they do it? They have 84 overs minimum. It's a strong ask but you never know. Stay tuned for the run chase!

PAKISTAN NEED 343 RUNS TO WIN! Strong reply by England with the bat. All their batsmen made their presence felt in this innings. Five of them registered half centuries. Alex Hales and Alastair Cook laid the foundation early on and then Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow and Moeen Ali scored crucial runs. Aggressive batting towards the end helped England post a strong total on the board.

Alastair Cook now sits on a sizeable lead of 311 and can use this opportunity to declare early. Pakistan are in serious trouble here, with a win seeming increasingly distant. It still remains a tight contest and conclusive result might not be on the cards. In this game of shifting fortunes, it is yet to be seen which team comes out on top. So, stay tuned as we take you through the coverage of this final day.

Welcome to the final day of the 3rd Test between England and Pakistan. What a shift in fortunes this match has seen! Yesterday, Pakistan looked to put a spoke in England's batting, but Moeen Ali and Jonny Bairstow rescued the hosts from a precarious position. Pakistan's bowlers harassed the batsmen from the start with Misbah-ul-Haq's plans of frustrating them bearing fruit early. The English, for their part, weathered it out and have come out ahead.
...Day 5, Session 1...

England have already set up a sizable lead but it looks like they would like to lengthen it even further. Pakistan's batsmen and bowlers will have a hard task cut out for them tomorrow. However, this match has swung back and forth throughout and it is beyond us to predict its outcome. Join us tomorrow for the final day's coverage of the Test, should be a thrilling finale. Until then... Cheers and take care!

The visitors seemed to have the batsmen figured out in the first two sessions, hemming them in and getting wickets when needed. In the latter half of the day, Pakistan's bowlers struggled against England's batsmen. Yasir Shah struck just as Ballance was looking comfortable, but none of the bowlers were unable to stop the flow of runs.

The tables turn once more! England have ended this session on a very good note, pushing their lead to an imposing 311. They were in a shaky position to begin with but with the arrival of Moeen Ali, the batting line-up has firmed up considerably. Bairstow and Moeen have set up a 132-run partnership that has been peppered with boundaries.

However, Pakistan got their breakthrough when Yasir Shah went around the wicket and dismissed Root on 62. Vince, after leading the hosts to a decent start, was also removed by a resurgent Amir. Can Pakistan close in for the kill or will England's trusty middle order get them out of the deep? Join us back shortly for the final session.

Evenly matched, the two sides are now balanced on a knife's edge and will want to put their best foot forward today. Pakistan have had the night to think about how they want to tackle the host's batsmen while England will be looking to lock down on their lead. Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the 3rd Test between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston. England have made a brilliant comeback with their bowling side nipping at the heels of the Pakistan's batsmen and ending the innings on what looked like a decent lead. The opening pair of Cook and Hales carried on the momentum to wipe out Pakistan's lead.
...Day 4, Session 1...

Now that England have reclaimed the lead by 17 runs, Pakistan will have to work on getting those wickets early. Join us at 1530 IST to find out who will take the upper hand in this evenly matched contest. Until then... Cheers and take care!

England made sure the openers registered their first ever 100-run stand and they have ended the day on a high. Alastair Cook and Alex Hales have both played respectably so far. Hales is showing a more conservative side than recent times while Cook has kept up his high run rate. With the duo sitting on half-centuries, it is likely that they will give the visitors a difficult time tomorrow as well.

The hosts kept up the momentum in the afternoon, with one wicket falling after another. However, Pakistan did try to put up a fight with Misbah posting a half-century and Sarfraz Ahmed putting up a decent score too. England brought the sting back into their pace attack today, keeping their lines tight and the batsmen on their toes.

It's been a good day for the Englishmen! They have finally come up with a fitting reply to the commanding performance put up by Pakistan in the previous two days. They began the day on a positive note, getting two crucial wickets in the morning session and widening the break in the visitor's batting line-up that was left at the end of yesterday's close.
